candidates.new:
BMI irq1_flip_go                \ grind: pending at a match (every flip field): taken (3), BPL's untaken 2 + 1
    JMP no_flip                     \ not pending (a stale match 256 fields on): no flip. These 3 bytes pay for the
.irq1_flip_go                       \ 3 the toggle below saves, so nothing after moves
    LDA #&0C                        \ R12: Displayed screen start address register (high)
    STA crtc_reg
    LDA flip_crtc_hi
    STA crtc_data
    LDA #&0D                        \ R13
    STA crtc_reg
    LDA flip_crtc_lo
    STA crtc_data
    LDA acccon
    EOR #&01                        \ grind: D toggles: flip_screen is always the screen not shown (render: back = shown_screen EOR 1)
    STA acccon                      \ D: which RAM the video shows
    AND #&01                        \ = flip_screen (0 or 1): the D bit just toggled to
    STA shown_screen
    STZ flip_pending                \ 65C02 opcode
candidates.summary: irq1_handler's flip: ACCCON's D bit is toggled (LDA acccon / EOR #1 / STA acccon) instead of masked and ORed with flip_screen (LDA / AND #&FE / ORA flip_screen / STA), 4 cycles and 3 bytes less, because flip_screen is always the screen not shown (render: back = shown_screen EOR 1) and D always equals shown_screen. The 3 bytes are spent on BMI irq1_flip_go / JMP no_flip in place of BPL no_flip (+1 cycle on the flip path, the JMP only for a stale match with nothing pending) so the block stays the same size and nothing after it (no_flip at &2A1C, the sky code's BPL cell at &3131) moves: the toggle alone would slide everything down 3 bytes and make cell's BPL cross a page (-6 to -7 cycles a pass). Built and measured on the unshifted DEBUG_LIVES build, 600 passes from 500, seed 1: interrupts 1496 -> 1492 cycles a pass; work (wait excluded) unchanged within 1, because the flip interrupt lands in the wait for the flip. Gains only where an interrupt falls in work.
candidates.equivalence: Entry: only from the fall-through of BNE no_flip / BIT flip_pending (the label irq1_flip_go is new, referenced only by the BMI). Not pending (BMI not taken): JMP no_flip, the same place BPL no_flip went; flags and registers there are all rewritten by BIT irq_owned, and nothing in the flip body is skipped or run differently. Pending: BMI taken, the body runs as before except ACCCON: the old code wrote (acccon AND &FE) OR flip_screen, the new writes acccon EOR 1. These are equal iff acccon bit 0 (D) = NOT flip_screen when a flip happens. (1) D = shown_screen always: D is written only here (with shown_screen = the new D, in the same interrupt), in render_reset (D=0 and STZ shown_screen) and render_to_main (D=0, STZ shown_screen, STZ flip_pending); every other ACCCON write is a read-modify-write of the X or Y bit (cpu_sees_back/main, unpack_for_play, kindcache_build) or render_reset's copy loop (acc_main/acc_shadow, D=0). (2) flip_screen is stored only at player_done (render.6502 557) as back, and back = shown_screen EOR 1 read after wait_for_flip returned, i.e. with flip_pending clear; flip_pending is set only by set_flip_field, after render_pass (render, so after player_done), and shown_screen changes only in this interrupt when pending is set (or in render_reset/render_to_main, which run on the main thread and clear pending), so between that read and the flip shown_screen cannot change: flip_screen = shown_screen EOR 1 = D EOR 1 at every flip. Then the new ACCCON is the same byte, A = it, AND #1 = D_new = flip_screen = what the old code stored in shown_screen; STZ flip_pending as before. Registers: A is dead after the STZ (the tail loads it), X and Y untouched, C is not read by anything on the path (the old C=1 was never used). The interrupt's timing before the T1 write and the palette writes is untouched (protected lines unchanged); the CRTC writes happen 1 cycle later.
candidates.relies_on: No page-crossing change: the block is byte-for-byte the same size (BPL 2 -> BMI 2 + JMP 3 = +3; AND #&FE 2 + ORA abs 3 -> EOR # 2 = -3), checked by assembling: irq1_flip_go &29F6, no_flip &2A1C, leave_irq1_handler_owned &2A35, so every address after it is as before; BNE no_flip (&29EC) still crosses into page &2A as it did (4 cycles taken); the new BMI (&29F1) reaches &29F6 in the same page. A shift of 2 or 3 bytes would have made the BPL cell branch at &3131 (about 10,000 taken executions in 1,500 passes) cross a page: that is why the bytes are not given back. Relies on the invariants D = shown_screen and flip_screen = shown_screen EOR 1 at a flip (argued in equivalence): the full-redraw oracle and passlock's shown screen would catch a flip that picked the wrong screen.
